name: Arcturus RL-2 'Bouncer'
description:
A magazine-fed semi-automatic carbine that fires rubber-composite projectiles at velocities calibrated to cause maximum pain with minimum penetration. The Bouncer's rounds are 18mm rubber-jacketed cylinders that deform on impact, spreading their kinetic energy across a larger surface area than conventional bullets. The result is a deep-tissue bruise that hurts for days but doesn't break the skin — in theory. In practice, the RL-2 at close range delivers impacts that crack ribs, rupture blood vessels, and cause internal bleeding that only becomes apparent hours later.

Arcturus designed the Bouncer for sustained riot suppression — the semi-automatic action and 20-round magazine allow operators to maintain a volume of fire comparable to conventional carbines without the political consequences of firing live ammunition. The weapon's effective range of 50 meters and its rapid-fire capability mean that a squad of four Bouncer-equipped operators can deliver the equivalent of a beating to an entire crowd simultaneously, from a safe distance.

The RL-2 has been involved in more civilian injury incidents than any other weapon system in GLMZ. Its less-lethal classification means it is deployed casually, frequently, and without the hesitation that accompanies firearms. Security personnel who would think twice before firing a bullet will empty a Bouncer magazine without a second thought, because the rounds are 'safe.' The cumulative medical data — 47 confirmed fatalities, over 3,000 serious injuries annually — tells a different story.
specifications:
caliber: 18mm rubber composite
action: Semi-automatic, gas-operated
magazine: 20 rounds
effective range: 50 meters
muzzle velocity: 90 m/s
impact energy: 35 joules (designed threshold)
weight: 3.1 kg
length: 680mm
tactical_use: Sustained riot suppression and crowd control. Operators engage crowds with rapid semi-automatic fire, targeting center mass to create pain compliance at volume. The 20-round magazine and semi-automatic action allow a tempo of fire that keeps crowds moving and prevents reorganization.
cultural_context: The Bouncer is the weapon that GLMZ's lower tiers encounter most frequently. It is the sound of a protest ending, the impact of a labor action being suppressed, the bruise that tells you the system noticed your dissent. Its rubber rounds don't kill often enough to make headlines, but they hurt consistently enough to make a point.
known_users: Corporate security riot teams (all major corponations)
GLMZ law enforcement crowd control units
Private security at labor dispute sites
story_hooks: Autopsy records from a protest suppression operation show that 12 of the RL-2 rounds recovered from casualties were not rubber-composite — they were lead-core rounds in rubber jackets, designed to look less-lethal while delivering ballistic impacts. Someone in the supply chain is loading kill rounds into riot guns.

An RL-2 has been modified to fire at twice the standard velocity — 180 m/s instead of 90 — turning every round into a potential skull-fracture. The modification is a simple spring swap that takes 30 seconds. Instructions have been posted on security forums, and someone is distributing modified springs to operators.
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions Kinetic Denial System KDS-4 'Bouncer'

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist carbine with a distinctly industrial aesthetic — all hard angles and purposeful geometry. The Bouncer resembles a conventional tactical rifle but with a noticeably robust, reinforced receiver and oversized gas system. Its silhouette is aggressive yet clinical, designed to project authority rather than lethality.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 680mm overall. Barrel: 410mm. Width at receiver: 65mm. Magazine well depth: 90mm.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced — 3.1kg distributed toward the receiver. Feels substantial in the hands, with a low center of gravity that encourages controlled rapid fire. The gas tube and piston system add noticeable heft forward of the charging handle.
physical_description.primary_material: Aluminum 7075-T6 receiver with polymer handguard and furniture. Steel barrel and gas tube. Reinforced polymer magazine well rated for sustained friction.
physical_description.finish: Tactical matte black with brushed steel accents on the barrel and receiver. Polymer components have a slightly textured finish to reduce glare. Wear patterns typical of heavy deployment: scuffed edges, scratched rail systems, abraded paint on the magazine well.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: matte black. Accents: gunmetal gray on barrel and charging handle. Safety selector and magazine release rendered in high-visibility orange.
physical_description.grip_texture: Aggressive rubberized grip with pronounced waffle-pattern texture. Molded to encourage a firm, aggressive purchase. Furniture is hard polymer — unpadded and utilitarian.
distinctive_features: Oversized gas block vented to manage higher-pressure impulses from composite rounds
18mm breech face markedly larger than conventional rifle bore to accommodate deformable projectiles
Magazine well reinforced with steel inserts to handle repeated loaded magazine impacts
Velocity indicator on receiver side — small numbered scale showing projected impact energy at various ranges
Integral rail system along receiver and handguard for mount points (optics, lights, additional grips)
Bold 'RL-2' designation stamped on both sides of receiver
Muzzle brake designed to scatter impact flash and dust, obscuring operator visibility during rapid fire
Magazine spring marked with wear grooves from high-velocity round cycling
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS logo stamped prominently on left receiver side. Serial number on bottom of receiver. 'LESS-LETHAL' and 'AUTHORIZED SECURITY USE ONLY' engraved on both sides of magazine well. Licensing compliance marks on the barrel.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained by standards of heavy-use equipment — regular cleaning evident in the receiver's finish, but the muzzle brake and furniture show carbon fouling and polymer discoloration. Magazines show extensive wear from field loading/unloading cycles. Paint chipped at edges where the weapon contacts vehicle mounts or riot shield racks.
